scope: A valid v3.5 unique-common-core sticky predecessor with complete target-component coverage. After conditioning on the unique common-core state, every connected component of the exact residual relation-overlap graph contains at most two target relations.

theorem.statement: Within the frozen scope, residual cross-coupling can be handled exactly by componentizing the conditioned residual overlap graph. Singleton residual components are projected locally. Two-relation residual components are solved by exactly one natural join on all shared residual variables followed by exact boundary projection. Component boundary carriers are stored additively, never as a Cartesian product.
theorem.pair_component_rule: Exactly one natural join per two-relation residual component; no join chain is permitted.
theorem.three_plus_rule: Any residual component containing three or more target relations returns OPEN_RESIDUAL_COMPONENT_GT2 before pair or chain materialization.
theorem.multiple_core_rule: Multiple surviving exact common-core states remain OPEN_NONUNIQUE_COMMON_CORE_SUPPORT and are outside this theorem.
theorem.reconstruction: Restore the unique common-core state, select stored original singleton rows or pair-row witnesses matching the transformed boundary assignment, merge disjoint residual-component assignments, then replay every original relation.
theorem.complexity: Residual graph construction is polynomial in explicit scope incidence. Singleton projection is linear in explicit rows. Each pair component performs one O(|R_i||R_j| * poly(scope)) exact join, bounded by a fixed polynomial in original explicit input length L. Component storage and solving are additive; no exponent depends on the number of residual components.
